entries.title: Quantity check that NaN walks straight through
entries.spec: Accept a quantity only if it is a whole number from 1 to 100. Return null when accepted, otherwise an error message.
entries.rootCause: Every comparison with NaN is false, so both guards fall through and the function returns null — meaning accepted. A range check written this way rejects -1 and 1e9 while waving through NaN, which then flows into arithmetic and poisons the total.
entries.fix: Reject non-numbers before the range test: `if (typeof q !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(q)) return "not a number";`

entries.title: Age gate that Infinity and "25" both pass
entries.spec: Accept an age only if it is a whole number from 0 to 120. Return null when accepted, otherwise an error message.
entries.rootCause: The string "25" also passes, because JavaScript coerces it for both comparisons. The check constrains a range without ever establishing that it was given a number, so non-numeric values are coerced into looking valid.
entries.fix: Establish the type first: `if (typeof age !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(age)) return "not a number";`

entries.title: Port validator with no upper bound for non-numbers
entries.spec: Accept a port only if it is a whole number from 1 to 65535. Return null when accepted, otherwise an error message.
entries.rootCause: The bounds are right, so this reads as correct on inspection. But NaN satisfies neither comparison, so an undefined port reaches the client as an accepted value and the failure surfaces later, somewhere unrelated.
entries.fix: Reject NaN explicitly: `if (!Number.isFinite(port)) return "not a number";`

entries.title: Fibonacci with a missing base case
entries.spec: Return the nth Fibonacci number, where fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1.
entries.bugClass: Recursion without a complete base case
entries.rootCause: The guard only covers n === 0. For n = 1 the function evaluates fib(-1), which is not covered, so recursion never terminates.

entries.title: Primality check that trusts its input
entries.spec: Return true if n is a prime number, false otherwise.
entries.rootCause: The early return for n < 2 returns true instead of false, so every value below 2 is reported as prime.

entries.title: GCD that cannot handle negative numbers
entries.spec: Return the greatest common divisor of two integers as a non-negative number.
entries.rootCause: The loop condition requires b > 0, so a negative b exits immediately and the function returns a instead of the true gcd.

entries.title: Sum that starts from the first element
entries.spec: Return the sum of all numbers in the array. The sum of an empty array is 0.
entries.bugClass: Initial value taken from user input
entries.rootCause: The accumulator is seeded with nums[0] rather than 0, so an empty array yields undefined instead of 0.

entries.title: Maximum of an array, uninitialised
entries.spec: Return the largest number in the array.
entries.rootCause: -Infinity is a sentinel for "no value yet", but it leaks out as the return value for an empty array.
entries.fix: Return undefined when the array is empty, or document that the input must be non-empty.

entries.title: Second largest that ignores duplicates
entries.spec: Return the second largest distinct number in the array, or null if there is none.
entries.rootCause: The else-branch accepts equal values, so a repeated maximum is reported as its own second largest.
entries.fix: Require v < first in the else-branch.

entries.title: String reverse that drops the last character
entries.spec: Return the input string with its characters in reverse order.
entries.rootCause: The loop stops one character early, so the final character is never copied. The bug is invisible for empty strings.

entries.title: Vowel counter with a shifted index
entries.spec: Count the vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in a string, case-insensitively.
entries.rootCause: Starting at index 1 skips the first character, and reading s[s.length] produces undefined, so .toLowerCase() throws.

entries.title: Array rotation with a naive modulo
entries.spec: Rotate an array to the right by k positions. A negative k rotates to the left. Return a new array.
entries.rootCause: In JavaScript -1 % 3 is -1, not 2, so slice receives a negative index and the rotation goes the wrong way.

entries.title: Sorted check with an inverted comparison
entries.spec: Return true if the numbers are in non-decreasing order.
entries.rootCause: The predicate marks any increase as unsorted. It returns true only for arrays that are already decreasing.

entries.title: Deduplication that reorders the result
entries.spec: Remove duplicate values, keeping the first occurrence of each and preserving the original order.
entries.rootCause: A Set preserves insertion order, but the trailing sort discards it. The result is correct as a multiset and wrong as a sequence.

entries.title: Binary search that returns the wrong index
entries.spec: Return the index of the first occurrence of target in nums, or -1 if it is absent.
entries.rootCause: The match branch returns mid + 1, shifting every hit one position to the right. It still returns -1 correctly for misses, which is why tests rarely catch it.

entries.title: Off-by-one that passed review and reached production
entries.spec: Return the index of the target in a sorted array, or -1 if it is absent.
entries.rootCause: The loop starts at index 1 and the array is scanned before index 0 is checked, so the first element is only handled by a special case that runs last. This is the shape of bug that code review does not catch: every individual line is defensible.
entries.fix: Scan from index 0 and drop the special case.
